# The e2e coverage guard states three different numbers for what one run covered

## Context

@neo-opus-vega routed me a receipt from PR #18510's `e2e-engine` job rather than a prescription — the runner's own line saying 85 of 105 spec files are excluded. Reconciling it against the job summary found that **the tier states three different numbers for the same fact**, and the most visible one is the optimistic one.

That matters more than ordinary drift because both statements live in the honesty guard: the machinery that exists precisely because `testIgnore` DESELECTS specs rather than skipping them, so a green check certifies less than it appears to. A guard whose only job is accurate counting is currently miscounting.

`Live latest-open sweep: checked the latest 20 open issues at 2026-09-08T23:57Z; no equivalent found.` A2A in-flight claim sweep over the last 12 messages: no overlapping `[lane-claim]`. This is my lane (#17853, #18493, #18507).

## The Problem

Measured on `dev`:

```
105  total e2e spec files
 85  excluded — no Brain checkout
  4  excluded — workstation OffscreenCanvas
  1  rendering/LivePreviewMultiWindow.spec.mjs
  1  portal/LearnLinkRoutingNL.spec.mjs
---
 14  actually selected      ->  91 excluded
```

Against that, the tier says:

| statement | source | value | correct? |
|---|---|---|---|
| *"This run covers **20**"* | `test/playwright/externalBrainSelection.mjs:74` | 20 | **no** — over-states by 6 files, 43% high |
| *"selected **14** of 105"* | `buildScripts/util/e2eCiSelection.mjs` summary header | 14 | yes |
| *"the **89** excluded files appear nowhere"* | `e2eCiSelection.mjs:160` | 89 | **no** — 105 − 14 = 91 |

**The wrong one is the one people read.** The `covers 20` line prints into the job log on every run. The accurate 14 lives in the step summary, which is not beside the green tick — which is exactly how @neo-opus-vega arrived at 20 while investigating in good faith.

## The Architectural Reality

- **`externalBrainSelection.mjs:67` `excludedSpecNotice({ignore, total})`** computes `covers ${total - ignore.length}`. That module knows only the Brain-gated exclusions. It cannot see the GPU-4 or the two individually-named files, so **it is asserting a total-coverage figure it is not positioned to compute.** The number is not stale; it is out of scope.
- **`e2eCiSelection.mjs:160`** interpolates `${ignored + gpu}` = 89. This module *does* know the rest: line 123 computes `expected = brainFree - gpu - EXCLUSIONS.length`. The prose sum simply omits `EXCLUSIONS.length`, so the sentence contradicts its own header two paragraphs above.
- The `--summary` step and the runtime notice are printed by different modules at different times, which is how they drifted without either being obviously wrong in isolation.

## The Fix

1. **`excludedSpecNotice` stops claiming total coverage.** It reports what it knows — how many files its own exclusion class removed and why — and does not compute a `covers N`. A module that cannot see every exclusion class must not publish the residual.
2. **`e2eCiSelection.mjs:160` derives the excluded count as `total - executed`** rather than summing named classes. Self-consistent by construction: when a future exclusion class is added, a sum silently under-reports while a subtraction cannot.
3. **The accurate figure becomes the loud one.** The `covers N of M` statement belongs where the runtime notice currently prints, sourced from the module that knows every class.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC-1** — no statement in the tier reports a coverage or exclusion figure computed from a subset of the exclusion classes. Verified by a test that adds a synthetic exclusion class and asserts every published number moves together.
- [ ] **AC-2** — the excluded count is derived by subtraction from the selected count, not by summing named classes. Red-first: adding an exclusion class without touching the prose must NOT be able to produce a self-inconsistent summary.
- [ ] **AC-3** — the run's log carries the accurate `N of M` figure, not only the step summary. Evidenced by a hosted run (the tier is dispatchable per #18505, so this is a probe, not a PR cycle).
- [ ] **AC-4** — the arithmetic is asserted against the real tree: an arm computes `total`, each exclusion class, and `executed` from the actual selection and pins that they reconcile. A hard-coded `14` would pass today and rot on the next spec added.

## Contract Ledger — the three reporting surfaces

| surface | who computes it | what it may state | what it may NOT state |
|---|---|---|---|
| runtime notice (`excludedSpecNotice`, prints in the log and locally) | `externalBrainSelection.mjs` — sees the Brain-gated class only | its own subtrahend (`N of M excluded`), that further classes follow, and that restoring the variable makes those N **eligible** | any coverage or survivor figure; any CI-only referent, since it prints on a developer's machine |
| coverage line (`coverageLine`, prints in the job log) | `e2eCiSelection.mjs` — sees every class | `N of M selected, M−N excluded` | — |
| step summary (`summary`) | `e2eCiSelection.mjs` — sees every class | the full account: header, every class, each individually excluded file with cause and owner | a residual computed by summing named classes |

**One invariant across all three:** a module that cannot see every exclusion class publishes its own subtrahend and never the remainder. The coverage line and the summary both derive from `populations()`, so they cannot disagree.

**Residual arithmetic:** always `total - executed`, never a sum of named classes. A corrected sum breaks again at the next class; a subtraction from operands the header already stands behind cannot.

## Out of Scope

- **Putting a Brain checkout on the runner.** That is the cost/scope question #18505's receipt raises and it belongs to @tobiu; it is also the wrong order — we should not buy coverage we cannot yet describe accurately.
- **The excluded specs themselves.** #18422 and #18427 own the two individually-named files; the 85 are #17844's population.
- **Changing what the tier selects.** This ticket changes only what it *says*.

## Avoided Traps

- **"Just fix the 89."** That is one of three statements and the least visible. Fixing only the arithmetic would leave the loud line still over-stating by 43%.
- **"Sum the classes correctly."** A corrected sum is still a sum, and the next exclusion class re-introduces the defect silently. Subtraction from the selected count cannot drift.
- **"The summary is right, so this is cosmetic."** The failure mode of a coverage guard is being believed. A reader who takes `covers 20` at face value concludes the dock's multi-window behaviour has CI coverage it does not have.
